rites.name: Valones
rites.text: A form of strike that lands only within a short reach of the wielder, close enough to touch. Such strikes pass through barriers and hit every foe inside that reach.

rites.name: Thiastasha
rites.text: Thiastasha is the concept of the Courts in Joradernath, the formal ground where divine trials are held and councils convene during the Age of the first sovereign. It is remembered as the force that binds promises and sets the thresholds of the doors between worlds.

rites.name: Elimiola
rites.text: Elimiola is a concept of Joradernath in the Courts, the principle of a bargain struck between a trial and the doors it opens. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, Elimiola was invoked to weigh which worlds would stay joined.

rites.name: Ilolanoma
rites.text: Ilolanoma is a concept of the Joradernath Weave, the planted lattice that the makers used to bind sleeping powers during the Seeding of the Holy Age. It names the moment when flame-temples and sworn orders first learned to call a sleeping power awake and turn it toward a single purpose.

rites.name: Corianium
rites.text: A tuned working that alters how much harm a bearer deals or suffers. It can sharpen the blow or soften the wound.

rites.name: Tinauntia
rites.text: A powerful technique that a fighter must build up over time before releasing it. Its readiness is displayed on a gauge that fills steadily.

rites.name: Telises
rites.text: A tactical strike that lands with extra force when it reaches a vulnerable point on a foe. Most practitioners aim for the head, while a few gifted fighters have other ways to trigger it.

rites.name: Valauria
rites.text: A temporary condition that settles upon a being for a brief span. It is usually cast by a skill, though certain blades can also impose it, and some workings join several such conditions together.

rites.name: Valeoles
rites.text: A bearer's form is altered for a brief span, bringing new arms or extra vigor that no binding or stun can break. The change ends when the bearer chooses to end it, when the time runs out, or when the reserves of the new form are spent.

rites.name: Valiastiles
rites.text: Each champion carries a personal gift that belongs to them alone. Its use is not spent from a supply, but is held back by recharge periods and a stored reserve. Such gifts fall silent when the bearer's mind is seized by a foreign will.

rites.name: Sistiallor
rites.text: A held working that lasts across a span of moments, breaking early if its bearer is struck by a seizing hex. Some such workings grant their bearer brief immunity to binding, and others lock out other crafts until they finish.

rites.name: Rernum
rites.text: Small boons that a fighter gains partway through a contest, each one sharpening a particular skill of their chosen champion. They open up as the struggle goes on, reshaping how each champion fights.

rites.name: Valaures
rites.text: Temporary constructs that a champion raises in a place, where they linger until shattered or they fade. Most of these constructs are not counted as champions and resist most lingering enchantments.

rites.name: Miasus
rites.text: A craft in which a single action touches every being inside a marked ring or zone at once, rather than one chosen target. Its users rely on it to command open space during clashes between groups.

rites.name: Ciantum
rites.text: A playful arcade rule that lightens the pull on everything, letting participants leap higher and float across the field in a shared challenge mode.

rites.name: Nillontum
rites.text: Quiet inner gifts that work without being called upon, shaping how a bearer moves and carries their craft. Some are shared by an entire calling, while others mark a single bearer's distinct method of acting.

rites.name: Oriantes
rites.text: A fighting art whose effects reach across a distance, either by hurling a missile or by producing an effect at a chosen spot. It stands opposed to close-quarters striking, and most techniques in the realm follow this form.

rites.name: Narium
rites.text: A restorative flow that mends a wielder's renewable vitality, drawn from charged crystals, sacred springs, and skilled helpers. Those who channel it gain power when they mend others who were struck.

rites.name: Brordestath
rites.text: Brordestath is a classified conditioning doctrine from the martial houses of Joradernath, which hones ordinary soldiers into swift, enduring fighters through a regimen of shifting tides and grafted resonance. Its graduates are feared less for their individual might than for their ability to outrun and outlast any force sent against them. The doctrine is quietly reviled by the civilian councils who fear what its veterans will do once the war ends.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a shared discipline of stillness and breath taught in the high monasteries of Varnhollow's eastern peaks, where practitioners learn to convert focused grief into kinetic force. Its adepts are known to dislodge boulders and split frozen rivers, though the discipline forbids using it against living settlements.

rites.name: Ashiazeth
rites.text: Ashiazeth is a concept of the Joradernath omniverse, personified as the branching doctrine that the Three Futures keep as a single chosen path among many. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is invoked as the principle that every outcome is shelved and waiting.
